title: Why factory farms are a major threat to food safety
summary:
Title: Why factory farms are a major threat to food safety

URL Source: https://www.foodsafetynews.com/2026/06/why-factory-farms-are-a-major-threat-to-food-safety/

Published Time: 2026-06-23T04:02:53.000Z

Markdown Content:
## Subscribe to Food Safety News

Get the free version of our newsletter. No spam ever, unsubscribe anytime.

By The Environmental Working Group

Every week, federal investigators track between 17 and 36[foodborne illness outbreaks](https://www.cdc.gov/foodborne-outbreaks/outbreaks/index.html?ref=foodsafetynews.com)that can cause extreme sickness and even death. Industrial livestock farming, also known as factory farming, is a main cause.

In 2019, the most recent year with complete data, the U.S. saw almost 10 million cases of foodborne illnesses, including almost 1,000 deaths, from E. coli, salmonella and other bacteria, according to the[Centers for Disease Control and Prevention](https://www.cdc.gov/food-safety/php/data-research/foodborne-illness-burden/index.html?ref=foodsafetynews.com).

The harmful bacteria can contaminate raw produce like cantaloupe,lettuce, and onions or more highly processed foods like meat, poultry and ice cream.

One cause is the way large factory farms operate, including their management of the waste they generate, according to the Food and Drug Administration.

Livestock waste can harbor many different types of bacteria, including a strain of E. coli that is particularly dangerous for humans. When bacteria from animal waste contaminate nearby fruit and vegetable crops, the people who eat them can get seriously sick.

title: Figures show higher rates of illness for older people in Scotland compared to other countries
summary:
Rates of food poisoning among older people appear to be higher in Scotland than in other countries, according to recent research.

Findings have helped Food Standards Scotland (FSS) clarify who is more likely to become ill and experience severe symptoms to tailor messaging accordingly.

Published Time: 2026-06-19T04:06:37.000Z

Markdown Content:
EU Commission considers more cereulide testing

![Image 1: Charity calls for improved infant formula controls in UK](https://storage.ghost.io/c/43/4e/434e508a-5e2f-4102-a53d-00bca10bb4bf/content/images/size/w30/2026/06/baby-infant-formula.png)

Published:June 19, 2026, 12:06 am

A charity in the United Kingdom has made several recommendations to regulators after the cereulide infant formula contamination incident.

First Steps Nutrition Trust said the situation exposed important weaknesses in the safety and security systems governing infant foods.

Contaminated products may have been on the market from May 2025 until the first Food Standards Agency (FSA) alert on Jan. 5, 2026. This raises questions about the adequacy of existing regulatory oversight, surveillance and incident response, said the public health nutrition charity.
